answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money; 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying below it; draws 8 Zoo cards, keeps 4 and discards 4; draws 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I, Animals in slot 1 and the other four randomly in the remaining slots. Appeal starts staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Setup C3: 1 active worker and remaining 3 lying down; D: Take 25 money; E: Draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4 ... discard ... 4; B: Animals card under the leftmost slot ... remaining 4 randomly ... side I; C1: Appeal ... start player ... 0 ... second ... 1 ... third ... 2 ... fourth ... 3.

answers.answer: Four-player games use the 4 topmost Base Conservation Project cards face up below the Association board; all other player counts use 3. In two-player games only, block the left level on the left face-up base project, the middle level on the middle project, the right level on the right project, and all three spaces in the donation area's left column; neither player may use them. The summary does not describe any blocked spaces for 3- or 4-player games. Reveal the initial six-card display after everyone has chosen their hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b: In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up ... otherwise the 3 topmost. Setup 5c: 2-player game only ... cover ... levels ... and ... three spaces in the left column ... blocked. Setup G: After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

answers.answer: After using a slot-4 card, remove it, shift all cards to the left of the empty slot one space right, and put the used card in slot 1. Action strength is set before the action starts. Each X-token spent adds +1 strength; spent tokens return to supply, any number may be spent, and no more than 5 may be held. Tokens gained during an action cannot boost that same action. Bonuses gained earlier in an action may be used later in that action, subject to paying each item before receiving its own benefits. An after-finishing effect resolves after the action is complete, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot ... and place the used card in slot 1. X-tokens: each token spent adds +1 strength ... never hold more than 5 ... set the strength before performing the action. After finishing effects: complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

answers.answer: No; doing nothing is not a legal turn action. Instead, if unable or unwilling to perform one of the five actions, take exactly 1 X-token. Still select an Action card, move it to slot 1 and shift the intervening cards right; strength and upgrade state do not matter. This alternative is unavailable when already holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: You may not do nothing ... Use the alternative X-token action. X-TOKEN action: take exactly 1 X-token ... select an Action card, move it to slot 1 ... If you already have 5 X-tokens, you cannot perform this action.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement, and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. The break happens after the current turn ends, so the triggering player completes that turn. Following a break triggered during a turn, play continues clockwise with the next player. The summary's end-game extra-turn rule applies only if the game end is triggered during a break, in which case all players take one more turn; it does not say that a break itself gives all players an extra turn.
answers.evidence: Break track: break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get 1 X-token ... Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. Break procedure: Play then continues clockwise with the next player. End of the game: if the end is triggered during a break, all players take one more turn.

answers.answer: Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck according to the slot-strength table (up to 3, with a possible discard) or snaps exactly 1 display card at strength 5 or more, regardless of reputation. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or from the display within reputation range in any order using its upgraded table; it snaps at strength 3 or more. The summary says the display is replenished at the end of the turn (and explicitly not until turn completion for side II). The hand limit is not enforced during a turn; cards are discarded down to the limit at breaks.
answers.evidence: Cards I: Advance the Break token 2 spaces ... draw from the deck ... maximum 3 ... or snap ... strength 5 or more ... regardless of your reputation. Cards II: Advance ... 2 spaces ... deck and/or from within reputation range ... Snapping ... strength 3. Special Rules: display ... do not replenish it until your entire turn is complete. Hand size ... enforced only at breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card on the folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. If at 15 and gaining more reputation, remain at 15 and gain 1 appeal for each additional reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Within reputation range = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. If your counter is on space 15 ... take 1 appeal per remaining reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than action strength. Build II builds any number of different buildings, total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in the same action. Each building costs 2 money per space, paid before placement. The first building must have at least one space on a map-border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces and do not extend beyond the map, overlap, or cover water/rock. Spaces with the restricted icon require upgraded Build. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately and once increases appeal by 1.
answers.evidence: Build I: exactly 1 ... size up to ... strength; Pay 2 money per space. Placement rules: first building ... border space; build adjacent ... restricted icon require upgraded Build; kiosk ... at least 3 spaces ... Each pavilion ... increases ... appeal by 1. Build II: as many different buildings ... maximum total size equal to strength.

answers.answer: Build I permits kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and one Petting Zoo per zoo. Build II additionally permits one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary per zoo (both size 5). The components include 4 of each special enclosure type: Petting Zoo, Reptile House, and Large Bird Aviary. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter only through Sponsor cards. When every map space except water and rock is covered, gain 7 appeal immediately; reaching restricted spaces requires upgraded Build, though the coverage may result from any effect.
answers.evidence: Components: 4× Petting Zoo, 4× Reptile House, 4× Large Bird Aviary. Build I available list ... Petting Zoo ... maximum 1. Build II: Large Bird Aviary and Reptile House ... maximum 1 each ... Unique buildings can never be built with this action ... full map ... immediately gain 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes: money, cards and newly activated workers gained earlier in an action may be used for later steps, and side-II Association tasks resolve in sequence so workers or other bonuses from an earlier task can support a later one. Each item must be paid before receiving its own benefits; animal costs must be fully payable before money from playing that animal is gained. For a Build II action, each building is paid separately before placement and placement bonuses are taken before the next building; after-finishing bonuses wait until the whole Build action ends. In Animals actions, ordinary effects resolve immediately, while after-finishing effects wait until the entire action and Action-card movement are complete. When effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order. For project support, the player may take the activated token bonus before or after the project reward.
answers.evidence: X-tokens: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps ... must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Animals: must be able to pay full cost first; after-finishing effects wait until the entire action is done. Build II: placement bonuses before ... next building, but hold after-finishing bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Multiple simultaneous effects ... owning player chooses the order.

answers.answer: For each animal, first meet all conditions on the card, then pay its cost. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon on the card, including multiple icons. Then place it in an eligible enclosure: any animal except a Petting Zoo animal can occupy an empty standard enclosure by itself if it is at least the required size; Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. All reptiles and some birds may instead use the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if suitable; mark the number of spaces shown on the card with player tokens, and insufficient remaining capacity rules out that option. Some animals require adjacent water/rock spaces; the requirements apply to special enclosures too. Gain appeal and other effects after placing the card. Ordinary effects resolve immediately (including before a second animal); after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action is complete. The summary does not specify a special occupancy procedure for a standard enclosure beyond flipping it to its occupied side.
answers.evidence: Animals I steps: check conditions; pay cost; partner zoo ... reduces ... 3 money per continent icon; fill an empty enclosure ... standard enclosure ... at least required size ... Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Special enclosures: mark ... spaces ... with player tokens ... water/rock requirements apply ... Effects: after finishing ... wait ... all other effects execute immediately.

answers.answer: Animals II allows display cards within reputation range as well as hand cards; pay an additional amount equal to the card's folder number. The two animals may be any mix of hand and display, and the display is not replenished until the turn ends. At strength 5 or more, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies. Animals with the upgrade-required icon may also be played.
answers.evidence: Animals II: may also play Animal cards from the display within your reputation range, paying ... folder number ... 2 animals may be any mix ... display is not replenished until your turn ends. Strength 5 or more ... first increase your reputation by 1 ... may also play animals ... upgrade-required icon.

answers.answer: Existing animals can move only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, and only once per building. Suitable animals (all reptiles and some birds) may move into their corresponding special enclosure, subject to its remaining capacity; each moved animal occupies the number of spaces shown on its card, marked with player tokens from the supply. For each animal moved, first flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure satisfying all requirements, including water/rock, back to empty; if none qualifies, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if no occupied enclosure meets even the size, flip none. Decide separately for each animal.
answers.evidence: Moving animals into a new special enclosure: allowed only immediately when you build the Reptile House / Large Bird Aviary, once per building. For each animal moved, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all its requirements ... if none ... size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none ... decide per animal.

answers.answer: Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, conservation project work 5. Side I performs exactly one task and requires at least one active worker; side II performs one or more different tasks with total task value at most the action strength, using 1 or 2 of your workers per task as applicable. If one of your workers is already on a task, repeating it requires placing 2 workers; if 3 of your workers are there, you cannot repeat until after the break. Other players' workers do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association I: exactly one task ... at least 1 active worker ... if 1 of your workers is already on that task, place 2 ... if 3 ... cannot ... until after the break. Other players' workers ... do not matter. Task strengths listed as 2, 3, 4, 5. Side II: one or more different ... 1 or 2 of your workers per task ... total value may not exceed strength.

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from the Association board and placed onto the lowest available spaces in their respective columns on your zoo map; take any printed placement bonus immediately. During breaks, replenish them so each is available exactly once, skipping items all players already have. Partner zoos must be from different continents, cannot exceed 4 total, and the third (or fourth) requires upgraded Association. Universities cannot be duplicated. Universities grant reputation and research icons; they are the only way to raise the hand limit to 5 (otherwise 3, checked at breaks). A partner zoo reduces animal costs by 3 per matching continent icon and provides that continent icon.
answers.evidence: Association tasks: take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty ... maximum 4 ... different continents ... third (or fourth) requires upgraded Association; university ... lowest available ... cannot take a duplicate. Universities ... only way to increase your hand limit to 5.

answers.answer: At strength 5, project work can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; with Association II it may also be played from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number. A new project goes in the leftmost space above the Association board and pushes others right. To support, meet an unoccupied condition and move one player token from the left edge of your zoo map onto that condition; each player may support each project only once. The token's bonus activates immediately, and may be taken before or after the project reward. When a new project exceeds the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project and return tokens on it to their owners' supplies, not to their zoo maps; their bonuses remain activated.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work: support a project already in play or play a card from your hand and support immediately. Support: fulfill a condition ... place 1 player token ... from the left edge ... may support each project only once ... token ... activates its bonus ... choose whether ... before or after project reward. Overflow: discard the rightmost card and return tokens ... to owners' supplies (not to zoo maps).

answers.answer: Yes. A Release into the Wild project requires the animal's standard-enclosure size to match the depicted size exactly, even if it could also live in a special enclosure. First lose only its printed appeal, before gaining conservation points; discard it and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If it can live in a special enclosure, remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens first if possible; otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or if none does, the smallest occupied enclosure meeting the size alone; if no occupied enclosure meets the size, flip none. A new Release project grants 1 reputation; supporting an existing one does not.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild: required standard size must match exactly ... First lose only the animal's printed appeal ... discard ... lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects ... remove ... special-enclosure tokens if possible; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else ... size alone, else none.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand when action strength is at least its level and conditions are met; alternatively, advance the Break token by strength and take that much money. Sponsors II may play one or more cards if strength +1 is at least the sum of their levels; cards may come from hand or display within reputation range, with the folder number paid as extra cost, and upgrade-required conditions are allowed. Resolve cards one by one, fully executing each instant effect (except after-finishing effects) before the next. The break-token alternative on side II pays money twice the movement amount. If only one step remains before the last space, the summary still says take the full money corresponding to strength on side I, even if movement does not need all those steps; side II doubles that money.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I: strength at least the card's level ... OR advance Break token ... strength and take that much money — full money even if ... doesn't need all the steps. Sponsors II: strength +1 ... sum of levels ... cards ... hand or display ... paying folder number ... execute ... before the next. Break-token option: take the money twice.

answers.answer: Break order: (1) discard to hand limit, normally 3 or 5 with the particular university; (2) return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; (3) recall all association workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; (4) discard display folders 1 and 2, slide the rest down and refill; (5) take income: appeal-track money, then kiosk income, then break-icon income on Sponsor cards and activated zoo-map bonuses; (6) reset the Break token. Each kiosk earns 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure (even empty), occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify. If several players take display cards during income, refill the display after each player; if order is needed, start with the break initiator (or affected player closest to them) and go clockwise.
answers.evidence: Break procedure lists hand limit, token return, Association board, display, income (appeal money; kiosk income; break-income icons), then break-track reset. Kiosk income: 1 money per ... unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion ... empty standard ... no income. Multiple players: refill the display after each player.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade one Action card or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, take 5 money or a Bonus token next to that space (the money option remains when tokens are gone). The first player to reach or exceed 10 has all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card; if no one reaches 10 before game end, everyone discards one before scoring. Check for game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until the end of your turn or a break to trigger it, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and everyone else takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation points. Victory points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player who supported the most projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation track: rewards at 2, 5 and 8, and 10. End of game: check at end of your own turn or during a break ... same scoring area, or pass one another ... appeal from another player's turn waits ... triggering player completes turn and others take one more turn. Final scoring: max 4 conservation points per card; VP = Appeal value − Target Number; tiebreak most projects, then share.
